pr_title: systemctl: show plain text files and arbitrary links in help
pr_body:
For file:// links, we reuse the machinery from 'systemctl cat' to just show a header and cat the file. (Man pages have their own header. But with plain-text files, it's better to show the file path/name.)

For all other links, which are primarily http:// and https://, we just show the link. The user can then ctrl-click and open the file it their browser. If we tried to open the files automatically, we'd would need to open many pages, and we'd need to figure out what browser to use, etc. When the user picks whether to open the file, this leads to a nicer user experience.

A bit of explicit flushing is needed to make sure that various outputs are not interleaved.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/29061.
pr_comments:
frankly, i am not convinced we need this at all. I for one think a clickable URL is a ton better than starting firefox or so here.

hence, maybe change the existing code to simply generate nice clickable links via that ANSI sequence for clickable links for the web stuff. and output that to stdout rather than stderr.

At least for me personally that sounds a ton more attractive, in particular as this would always open the urls on my local machine, rather than remotely.

It could be a good start, but with the "spoiled" audience in this era it might be wanted to auto-open in `www-browser`/`x-www-browser` which are set in debian-like distro's to the browser of choice...
_(Maybe more or all distro's my head hurts at moment)_

Yeah, I got so hung up on displaying text files that I didn't consider that some people might link pdfs or other things. I changed this to show links. Seems to be work nicely for text files, pdfs, http and https links. For stuff like `file:///bin/sh`, the user just gets an error popup, which seems to be the most appropriate.

issue_context.title: [RFE] systemctl help (more as man pages)
issue_context.body:
- https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/src/systemctl/systemctl-show.c#L831-L835
https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/47d8770aace000e0bfcc68ecf7d84e0bd9886431/src/systemctl/systemctl-show.c#L831-L835

Could this be enhanced to allow `file:`, `http:` and `https:` :thinking: 
The more and more people create units, the more they like to add links to some documentation to accompany the unit...

- For `file:` you could use [the default pager](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/src/shared/pager.c) to display the plain text contents of the file.
- For `http:` and `https:` you could possibly make use of an environment variable, to select the viewer to launch?
fe `${SYSTEMD_HELP_VIEWER}`, `${SYSTEMD_HELP_ONLINE_VIEWER}` or similar...
Which defaults to lets say `www-browser` or `x-www-browser` or the value from `xdg-settings get default-web-browser`.
(see also https://linuxconfig.org/how-to-set-browser-environment-variable-on-linux)
comments:
> * For `file:` you could use [the default pager](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/main/src/shared/pager.c) to display the plain text contents of the file

why do you think that would be appropriate? `file:` is a (pseudo-) protocol, and not a hint about the file format used. the referenced doc could be an html or PDF or so, you really shouldn't dump that in a pager.

@poettering 
> why do you think that would be appropriate? `file:` is a (pseudo-) protocol, and not a hint about the file format used.

I know... But it is mostly, or will be, used to link to local text/markdown files.
(Extra comment: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/29133#discussion_r1321616585)

> the referenced doc could be an html or PDF or so, you really shouldn't dump that in a pager.

If you find it too dangerous, you could check the extension or even check the mime-type of the file pointed at, before feeding it to the pager...

Besides, it's the responsibility of the Unit writer to point the documentation using `file:` to a **text file** fit for display in the default pager right?

review_comments:
As per https://gist.github.com/egmontkob/eb114294efbcd5adb1944c9f3cb5feda#file-uris-and-the-hostname these urls should probably be rewritten so that: `file:///foo/bar` becomes `file://gethostname()/foo/bar`, for compat with ssh remoting.

Also, I think we should also urlify http/https links here (but of course not rewrite them)

Update to use `terminal_urlify_path()` which inserts the hostname.

I didn't add urlification of http/https links: this would additional code, which doesn't seem necessary. Terminal emulators handle http/https/ftp and similar links on their own, so if we don't do anything, the user gets the correct behaviour anyway. I adjusted the commit message to mention this.

Yes, see the commit message ;)
We use printf/puts here, but also write the man page from stdout from a child process. Without the appropriate flushing, I was getting interleaved output. (Or more precisely, not interleaved, but in the wrong order.)
